x: This is the leg where the race can be won and lost, and names such as Hyman (who produced a fantastic new record - 34 seconds better than his own previous best), Wilkinson, Perry, North, Reed, Edmonds, Hogan and Foord appeared - enough to frighten the stoutest of hearts.

Perry, Strudwick, Badgery and Cope not only led from start to finish but they smashed Coventry's course record by no less than 48 seconds. Bill Lucas set the race in motion on this windy autumnal Saturday and Mitcham, Ilford, Watford, Q.P.H. and Essex Beagles were soon fighting it out at the front.
With two laps to go he looked stronger than ever and simply tore past Glamorgan's McAndrew to reach sixth place at the bell with the bearded Perry 30yds ahead.
With the opposition nicely strung out ahead Geoff raced through the field, catching the Derby runner (Calladine) after only 3 miles and only just failing to beat Perry of Birchfield for second place.
